project_specification.overview: A post-build documentation agent system for AutoForge that automatically generates a complete knowledge base, tutorial video scripts, and an embedded in-app help system for every AutoForge-built project. Runs after all features pass, producing professional onboarding materials so every app ships with documentation out of the box. Offered as a tiered premium add-on ($49-99 per project) that differentiates AutoForge from competitors that ship code with no docs.

frontend.state_management: TanStack Query, React hooks and context

additional.mcp: Feature MCP server (read-only), Playwright MCP server
additional.testing: ruff (Python lint), npm run lint + npm run build (TypeScript), Playwright e2e

prerequisites.environment_setup: - Python 3.11+ with existing AutoForge venv - Node.js 20+ for UI development - Existing AutoForge installation with all dependencies - Playwright MCP server available for browser automation - Claude Agent SDK configured

core_features.agent_prompt_and_template: - Create knowledge base prompt template at .claude/templates/knowledge_base_prompt.template.md with documentation generation instructions, screenshot conventions, and MCP tool reference - Add get_knowledge_base_prompt() to prompts.py that loads the template with tier-aware section injection following the existing fallback chain (project-specific then base template), including _get_tutorial_script_section() for full/premium tiers and _get_in_app_help_section() for premium tier only
core_features.agent_infrastructure: - Register knowledge-base as a valid agent-type choice in autonomous_agent_demo.py with --kb-tier flag (basic/full/premium) and --kb-only flag for standalone doc generation on already-built projects - Configure client.py to provide the KB agent with read-only feature MCP tools (feature_get_stats, feature_get_by_id, feature_get_summary, feature_get_graph, feature_get_ready), built-in tools (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob), and Playwright MCP server, excluding all feature mutation tools - Add _check_knowledge_base_ready() to parallel_orchestrator.py that detects when all features are passing and spawns the KB agent with dynamic turn budget based on tier (200 base, 250 full, 280 premium) - Extend process_manager.py to support knowledge-base agent process lifecycle including start, stop, and status tracking, running in parallel with QA agent without file conflicts
core_features.server_api: - Add POST /api/projects/{project_name}/knowledge-base endpoint that accepts tier selection in request body, starts the KB agent, and returns status with agent_type, tier, and estimated_turns - Add GET /api/projects/{project_name}/knowledge-base/status endpoint that returns generation progress including features_documented, features_total, screenshots_taken, scripts_generated, output_path, and completed_at timestamp - Emit kb_progress events via the existing WebSocket at /ws/projects/{project_name} with feature documentation progress and screenshot capture events
core_features.ui_data_layer: - Add KBAgentType, KBTier, KBStatus, KBStartRequest, and KBStartResponse TypeScript types to types.ts, API client functions (startKnowledgeBase, getKnowledgeBaseStatus) to api.ts, and React Query hooks (useStartKnowledgeBase, useKnowledgeBaseStatus) to useProjects.ts
core_features.ui_components: - Add a Knowledge Base section to SettingsModal.tsx with auto-generate toggle checkbox and tier dropdown (Basic $49 / Full $79 / Premium $99) following existing settings section patterns - Add Sage mascot (book/scroll theme) to AgentMissionControl.tsx for the knowledge-base agent with Reading, Writing, and Screenshotting states displayed alongside existing mascots (Spark, Fizz, Octo, Hoot, Buzz) - Add a Docs tab to the project view tab navigation (alongside Kanban, Graph, Terminal) showing KB generation status card with progress bar and action buttons (Start, Stop, Regenerate) - Display a docs file browser within the Docs tab showing the generated docs tree (index.md, features/, api/, screenshots/) with inline markdown preview and download-as-zip button
core_features.edge_cases_and_resilience: - Handle authenticated apps by checking for login pages, searching for test/seed credentials (.env, seed files, fixtures), and creating a test account via signup flow if no credentials are found - Handle large projects (100+ features) by documenting in priority order and generating summary-only docs (title + description, no screenshots) for remaining features when approaching the turn budget limit - Return 409 Conflict from the KB start endpoint when generation is already running for a project, preventing duplicate agent spawns - Recover gracefully when the KB agent crashes mid-generation by updating the knowledge_base_runs status to failed with error_message and exposing a retry action in the UI

tables.knowledge_base_runs: - id (INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT) - project_name (TEXT NOT NULL, references project registry by name - not a DB FK since projects live in ~/.autoforge/registry.db) - tier (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'basic', CHECK IN ('basic', 'full', 'premium')) - status (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending', CHECK IN ('pending', 'running', 'completed', 'failed')) - features_documented (INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0) - features_total (INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0) - screenshots_taken (INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0) - scripts_generated (INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0) - output_path (TEXT) - error_message (TEXT) - started_at (TEXT) - completed_at (TEXT) - created_at (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - updated_at (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)

api_endpoints_summary.knowledge_base: - POST /api/projects/{project_name}/knowledge-base (start KB generation with tier) - GET /api/projects/{project_name}/knowledge-base/status (get current generation status and progress) - GET /api/projects/{project_name}/knowledge-base/history (list all KB runs for this project) - POST /api/projects/{project_name}/knowledge-base/stop (stop a running KB agent) - POST /api/projects/{project_name}/knowledge-base/regenerate (re-run KB generation, clearing previous output) - GET /api/projects/{project_name}/knowledge-base/download (download generated docs as zip)

ui_layout.main_structure: - Existing AutoForge UI layout with header, sidebar project list, and main content area - New Docs tab added to project view tab bar (Kanban | Graph | Terminal | Docs) - Settings modal gains Knowledge Base section - Agent Mission Control gains Sage mascot slot
ui_layout.docs_tab_layout: - Status card at top showing generation state, tier, and progress bar - Action buttons row: Start/Regenerate, Stop, Download - File browser below showing generated docs tree (index.md, features/, api/, screenshots/) - Markdown preview panel for selected doc file

design_system.color_palette: - Use existing AutoForge neobrutalism design system - KB-specific accent: Purple/indigo for Sage mascot and Docs tab indicator - Progress states: --color-neo-pending (yellow), --color-neo-progress (cyan), --color-neo-done (green)
design_system.typography: - Follow existing AutoForge typography (system fonts, font-semibold headings)
design_system.spacing: - Follow existing AutoForge spacing scale (4px base unit) - Docs tab layout uses standard content padding (p-4 / p-6) - File browser items use compact spacing (py-1 px-2) - Status card and action buttons use standard gap-3 spacing

ui_ux_standards.banned_patterns: - alert(), confirm(), prompt() - Use modals and toasts instead - Text-only empty states - Use EmptyState component with icon + CTA - Loading states that just say "Loading..." - Use skeleton loaders - Delete without confirmation - Always use ConfirmModal - Raw timestamps - Format as relative time
ui_ux_standards.required_components: - Use existing AutoForge UI components (Modal, Toast, Skeleton, EmptyState, ErrorBoundary) - Progress bar component for KB generation tracking - File tree component for docs browsing
ui_ux_standards.page_patterns: - Docs tab follows existing tab pattern in project dashboard - Settings additions follow existing SettingsModal section pattern - Mission Control additions follow existing mascot card pattern
ui_ux_standards.feedback_protocol: - KB start: toast confirmation + progress tracking begins - KB complete: toast notification + Docs tab shows results - KB failed: error toast + error details in status card + retry button

coding_standards.architecture: - Python: New router in server/routers/ or extensions to server/routers/agent.py - Python: New service logic in server/services/process_manager.py (extend existing) - Python: Prompt functions in prompts.py (extend existing) - TypeScript: Types in ui/src/lib/types.ts, API in ui/src/lib/api.ts, hooks in ui/src/hooks/ - TypeScript: Components in ui/src/components/ - Follow existing patterns in each file - match code style and conventions
coding_standards.testing: - Python: ruff check . must pass - TypeScript: npm run lint and npm run build must pass - New endpoints should be testable via curl/httpie
coding_standards.error_handling: - KB agent failures logged and surfaced via status API - WebSocket errors handled gracefully with reconnection - Process manager handles agent crashes (existing pattern)

key_interactions.auto_generate_kb_flow: 1. User enables "Auto-generate after build" in Settings > Knowledge Base 2. User selects tier (Basic/Full/Premium) 3. Build completes - all features pass 4. Orchestrator detects completion and spawns knowledge-base agent 5. Sage mascot appears in Agent Mission Control with "Reading" state 6. WebSocket emits kb_progress events as features are documented 7. Docs tab shows live progress bar 8. Agent completes - toast notification, Docs tab shows generated files 9. User browses docs in-app or downloads as zip
key_interactions.manual_kb_generation_flow: 1. User navigates to project dashboard Docs tab 2. User sees empty state with "Generate Knowledge Base" CTA 3. User selects tier from dropdown and clicks Generate 4. POST /api/projects/{name}/knowledge-base fires 5. Progress tracking begins, Sage mascot appears 6. On completion, docs file tree populates 7. User clicks a doc file to preview markdown content
key_interactions.regenerate_docs_flow: 1. User has existing generated docs but wants to update 2. User clicks Regenerate in Docs tab 3. ConfirmModal warns that existing docs will be replaced 4. User confirms, KB agent re-runs 5. New docs replace old docs, git commit created
